ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: Locusts have stripped the fields of {PEOPLE}.

lines.li: [them] The locusts took our fields in a single afternoon.
[us] All of them?
[them,their:lowtech] Every one, and the old women say they've never seen a cloud so wide.
[them] Every one around {SITUATIONPLACE}, and the swarm hasn't settled yet.
[us] Which way is it heading?
[them] Wherever the wind says, so keep an eye on the sky.
[them] The river came up in the night at {SITUATIONPLACE}, and it took a lot with it.
[us] I'm sorry, is anyone you know hurt?
[them] We're still counting what it took, and I'd rather not guess.
[us] If you need timber for rebuilding, ask us.
[them,their:tribal] I will carry your words back to the elders.
[them] I'll carry that home, thank you.
[them] No rain at home for months, they're calling it {SITUATION}.
[us] How are the fields holding up?
[them,their:lowtech] The wheat stands white, and the herders walk farther every day for water.
[them] Dry as old bread, and the wells are low.
[us] I hope the rains come soon.
[them,their:tribal] We dance for it every night, and the sky only watches.
[them] So does everyone, it's all anyone talks about.
[them] {SITUATION} is in our herds, they're burning carcasses outside the walls.
[us] Can people catch it?
[them] No, thank the stars, but it takes the milk, the meat and the plow oxen.
[us,colony:animals] Then we'll keep our animals well away from yours, just in case.
[us] Then I hope it burns itself out soon.
[them] Nobody even knows where it started, so that's all anyone can do.
[them] The fire at {SITUATIONPLACE} took more than we can count yet.
[us] I'm sorry, what will you need most?
[them] Timber, and someone who knows roofs.
[us] We'll see what we can spare.
[them] People will know whose timber is in the new walls.
[them] They're leaving {SITUATIONPLACE}, the whole town, carts and all.
[us] Where will they go?
[them] Wherever will have them, and not everyone has somewhere.
[us] Some may come this way, then.
[them] Some will, and what they leave behind is anyone's to take.
[them] We're in mourning at home, {SITUATION} has died.
[us] I'm sorry, who was {SITUATION}?
[them] Someone half the region knew, and the other half knew someone they'd helped.
[us] Then it's a loss for everyone.
[them,their:tribal] It is, and we will sing the name for a whole moon.
[them] It is, and the mourners will be on the roads for a while.
[them] A whole household was cast out of {SITUATIONPLACE}, given a day to leave.
[us] For what?
[them] Siding with the wrong cousin, or speaking too loud, it depends who tells it.
[us] Will they come this way?
[them] Some will, and our people won't thank anyone who takes them in.
[them] We're rebuilding at home, and everyone is short of timber and patience.
[us] How far along are you?
[them] Far enough to see the shape of it, and a long way from done.
[us] Ask if you need hands.
[them] Nobody with sense takes the road from {SITUATIONPLACE} now.
[us] Bandits?
[them] Bandits, and twice now they've taken the drivers along with the carts.
[us] Then I'm glad you got here in one piece.
[them,role:trader] So is my purse.
[them] So am I, believe me.
[them,their:lowtech] There's a chain across the road at {SITUATIONPLACE} and a man with a box beside it.
[them] There's a toll on the road at {SITUATIONPLACE} now, and nobody's happy about it.
[us] What does it cost to pass?
[them] More every month, and the traders are going the long way round.
[us] Then I'm glad we're on this side of it.
[them,their:lowtech] The mines have flooded, and the smiths at home are melting down old plowshares.
[them] Iron's gone scarce at home, and the smiths are paying whatever they must.
[us] What's it fetching?
[them] More than you'd believe, so if you've any to spare, I know buyers.
[them] {SITUATION} has failed, after forty years, and its drivers haven't been paid.
[us] What will that do to prices?
[them] Some things will go cheap as the stock is sold, and some you won't find at all.
[us] Then we'll keep our eyes open.
[them,role:trader] Keep them on me, I'll have the bargains first.
[them] Everyone will, it's that kind of season.
[them] Every inn on the road is full of merchants this season.
[us] Good for business.
[them,role:trader] Good for mine, and bad for my sleep.
[them] Good for some, and crowded for everyone else.
[them] Word at home is that your stalls are worth the walk.
[us] We're glad to hear it.
[them,role:trader] Then don't sell it all before I've had a look.
[them] Put your best out in the mornings, that's when the buyers come.
[them] The orbital lanes are crowded this season, every ship has something to sell.
[us] What are they selling?
[them,their:hightech] Everything, at prices that come down if you let them hail twice.
[them] Everything, at prices that come down if you wait.
[them] They're building {SITUATION} right past your land, did you know?
[us] We've heard it will pass close.
[them] When it opens, you'll have more traders than you know what to do with.
[us] We'll learn.
[them] The old road's open again, and every caravan on it is in a hurry.
[us] Good news for us, then.
[them] For a few weeks you'll be on the busiest road in the region.
[them] The lakes have frozen hard enough for sledges, and there's an ice road now.
[us] Is it safe?
[them] Safe until the thaw, and when the thaw comes, it comes quickly.
[us] Then I hope nobody's out on it that day.
[them] Carts of ours go past your gate most days now.
[us] And some of them turn in.
[them] Some of them, and some of them you'll wish hadn't.
[them] Our road wardens would like a post by your land, a fire and a few beds.
[us] And what would they want of us?
[them] Only the ground, and they'd ride out against anything that came up the road.
[us] It's worth thinking about.
[them] {SITUATIONPLACE} is growing fast, a smithy, two inns and a market.
[us] We're not the only ones on this road anymore.
[them] No, but you're the older one, and people remember that.
[them] Some of ours have settled not far from you, at {SITUATIONPLACE}.
[us] So we've heard.
[them] I hope you'll be friends, the land is wide enough for both.
[us] That depends on them as much as on us.
[them] Fair, and I'll tell them you said so.
[them] We've founded a new town, {SITUATIONPLACE}, and it's short of nearly everything.
[us] Congratulations, what does it need most?
[them] Timber, mostly, and neighbors to trade with.
[us] We might manage both.
[them,their:tribal] Then the new fires will know your name.
[them] Then you'll be welcome there.
[them] Half our town has gone off panning for gold, the blacksmith included.
[us] Has anyone found any?
[them] I hear plenty of talk and see very little gold.
[us] Not tempted yourself?
[them,role:trader] I sell them beans and rope, which is the surest gold there is.
[them] Tempted, but I like my feet dry.
[them] Everyone with a pick is out looking for silver since the strike.
[us] Any of them looking at our hills?
[them] Some of them, so keep an eye on who's digging where.
[them] The fields at home are heavier than anyone can remember.
[us] A good year, then.
[them] A good year, grain cheap, and not enough hands to bring it in.
[us,colony:hungry] We could use some of that grain, if you're selling.
[us] Then may it all get in before the weather turns.
[them] It will, if we have to cut it by lantern light.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: A ship, {SITUATION}, has come down near {SITUATIONPLACE}.

lines.li: [them] {SITUATION} came down in the hills past {SITUATIONPLACE}, a whole ship.
[us] Were there survivors?
[them] Nobody knows yet, but every salvager for a hundred miles is on the way.
[us] I hope they find someone alive in it.
[them,their:hightech] So do I, though most of them are hoping for parts.
[them] So do I, but most of them came for what they can carry.
[them] Our diggers broke into {SITUATION}, and the lights came on by themselves.
[us] Who built it?
[them] Nobody living knows, and half the region wants it filled in again.
[us] And the other half?
[them] The other half wants to know what's behind the deeper door.
[us] I think I'm with the first half.
[them,their:tribal,situation:theirs] The great herds are moving, and every hunter at home has gone out.
[them] The great herds are moving this year, the ground shakes at dusk.
[us] We've heard the talk, and we're keeping watch.
[them] There's meat for anyone who wants it, and trouble for anyone in the way.
[them] There are beasts about that even our old hunters can't name.
[us] Dangerous?
[them] Some are, some aren't, and nobody wants to find out which the hard way.
[us,us:best:Animals] I'd like a closer look at one, carefully.
[us] Then we'll give them room.
[them] Our drovers are walking the herds to market, you'll hear the bells first.
[us] Will they come by here?
[them] Some roads pass close, and they'll want grass and water.
[us] Water they can have, the grass we'll talk about.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: {SITUATION}, an old thrumbo, walks the hills of {PEOPLE}.

lines.li: [them] {SITUATION} has come down into our hills, the oldest thrumbo anyone has seen.
[us] Is it dangerous?
[them] Only to fools who go after its horn.
[us] It must be worth a fortune.
[them,their:lowtech] The elders say even thinking that brings bad luck.
[them] It is, and our people would never forgive whoever took it.
[them] What do you make of {SITUATION}, up there every night?
[us] Some say it means luck, and some say the opposite.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say war, or sickness, or a fat harvest, depending on the elder.
[them] At home they argue every night whether it means war, plague or a good harvest.
[us] I hope it's the harvest.
[them] The ley lines are restless, and our mages have shut their towers.
[us] Is it dangerous?
[them] Spells go wrong, and some go far too right.
[us] I'll stay clear of anything that glows, then.
[them] I hear the fish are running in your water.
[us] Every line comes up heavy this week.
[them] Then I know what I'd be doing, if I lived here.
[them] Have you heard about the healer going from town to town?
[us] A little, is it true what they say?
[them] I've heard a dozen stories, and even half of them would be a wonder.
[us,us:best:Medicine] I'd give a lot to watch someone like that at work.
[us] I'd like to see that for myself.
[them] Then get in line before dawn, everybody else does.
[them] {SITUATION} is on the road this season, and every hall is full.
[us] Who?
[them] The best known voice in the region, how have you not heard?
[us] We're a long way from the halls.
[them] There's a song going round about places like yours, you know.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Have you heard of {SITUATION}, and the people following her?
[us] A little, what do they want?
[them] To give away one thing you don't need, and feed whoever comes to the door.
[us] That sounds almost kind.
[them] Not to me, but the ones in charge at home are nervous.
[them] {SITUATION} is camped a day's march from here, and they're all sellswords.
[us] We've heard.
[them] Good fighters, I'm told, and not particular about who pays.
[us] That's what worries me.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: Riders of {PEOPLE} have killed the bandit lord {SITUATION}.

lines.li: [them] Have you heard, {SITUATION} is dead, and our riders did it.
[us] The bandit lord?
[them] The very one, run down at a ford, and the band is coming apart.
[us] Will the roads be safer now?
[them] Safer, once the stragglers find somewhere to go.
[us] Or someone new to follow.
[them] You'll have heard of {SITUATION}, I suppose.
[us] The warband?
[them] Every raid brings it more riders, so I travel by daylight.
[us] Keep your eyes open on the way home.
[them] I always do, and twice as wide this season.
[them] The clans are gathering, and the warbands are all on the road.
[us] Should we be worried?
[them,situation:theirs] Not of me, but keep your people close at night all the same.
[them] Keep your people close at night, and you'll likely be fine.
[them] We've a new {LEADERTITLE} now, {LEADER}, and people are still getting used to it.
[us] What do your traders make of {LEADER}?
[them] Every trader has an opinion, and every opinion is different.
[us] And yours?
[them,their:empire] Mine is that it isn't my place to have one.
[them] Mine is that I'll keep it to myself for now.
[them] Two claim the seat at home, and everyone is choosing a side.
[us] Which side are you on?
[them,them:kind] The side that ends it without blood.
[them] The side that wins, if I'm lucky.
[us] I hope it's settled quickly.
[them] It will be, one way or the other, and soon.
[them] {SITUATION} has two families at home at each other's throats.
[us] Over what?
[them] It started small, as these things do, and then someone drew a knife.
[us] I'll keep out of it, then.
[them] Wise, though both families will try to drag you in.
[them] It began as {SITUATION}, and now whole markets are closed over it.
[us] Nobody's come to blows, I hope?
[them] Not yet, they're counting the cost in silver instead.
[us] That's the better way to count it.
[them] Our preachers and theirs are shouting at each other from every market box.
[us] Only words, I hope.
[them] Only words, so far, and plenty of them.
[us] Words I can live with.
[them] Our people are tired enough of the war to talk, for once.
[us] Do you think it will come to peace?
[them] Maybe, if they find someone both sides half trust to host the talks.
[us] That's a rare thing to find.
[them] Rarer than peace, some days.
[them] {SITUATION} meets at {SITUATIONPLACE}, and this time you've been asked to send someone.
[us] What's to be settled?
[them] Grazing, roads, old debts, and the high pastures most of all.
[us] We'll think about who to send.
[them] Send someone who can sit through a long day of arguing.
[them] A circuit judge has come to {SITUATIONPLACE}, and every old quarrel is on its way there.
[us] Any of them ours?
[them] Only if you've a grievance to bring, and most people do.
[them] A great lord of ours is making a progress through the region, banners and all.
[us] Will it pass near here?
[them] Within a morning's walk, so polish whatever you have that shines.
[us] We'll find something.
[them] The levy has every steward in the region counting silver twice.
[us] Are we expected to give?
[them,their:empire] Expected is a strong word, remembered is the word the court uses.
[them] Expected is a strong word, remembered is the word they use.
[them] There's a price on every deserter brought back, if you see any.
[us] What did they do?
[them] Walked away from their posts, and the Empire doesn't forgive that.
[us] Some of them must only be tired.
[them,their:empire] Tired or not, they swore an oath.
[them] Some of them, and some took their gear along.
[them] {SITUATION} has every road full of canvassers.
[us] Who do you favor?
[them] The old families want things as they are, and the reformers want bread and land.
[us] And you?
[them] I want the shouting to stop, which no candidate offers.
[them] Have you heard about {SITUATION}, the biggest in years?
[us] Tell me about it.
[them] Contests on the green, the best shot, the best cook and the finest work.
[us,us:best:Cooking] I might fancy my chances with the cooking.
[us,us:best:Shooting] I might fancy my chances with a target.
[us] It sounds like quite a day.
[them] Then come, it's a week of days and every one of them loud.
[them] Our faithful are walking to the old shrine, and the roads are full of songs.
[us] Do many pass this way?
[them] Enough that a bowl of soup by the road would be remembered.
[us] We'll see what we can do.
[them] It's {SITUATION} at home, debts forgiven and every traveler fed.
[us] That's a generous custom.
[them] It is, and we'll see which neighbors keep it with us.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and everyone's still arguing about the prizes.
[us] Who's arguing?
[them] Everyone who didn't win, which is nearly everyone.
[us] {ENDED} is gone from the sky, then.
[them] Gone, and the arguing about what it meant has only started.
[us] Nothing terrible has happened yet.
[them] Give the arguing time.
[them] {ENDED} has moved on from our halls, but everyone still hums the songs.
[us] Even the one about places like ours?
[them] That one most of all, the children shout it in the streets.
[them] We've laid {ENDED} to rest, and the mourners have gone home.
[us] How is everyone?
[them] Lighter, a little, and still telling stories about {ENDED}.
[us] That's the best way to keep someone.
[us] What became of {ENDED}?
[them] The talk has died down, and the roads around home are quieter.
[us] Do you miss it?
[them] Some do, and some are glad of the quiet.
[them] {ENDED} has gone from our hills, one way or another.
[us] Do you know which way?
[them] I'd rather not, if it's all the same to you.
[them] The salvagers have picked {ENDED} nearly clean, I hear.
[us] All of it?
[them] All that could be carried, and the rest will rust where it fell.
[them] {ENDED} is gone from the region, one way or another.
[us] Nobody's sorry, I take it.
[them] Nobody's saying so out loud.
[them] The contest for the seat is settled at last.
[us] Peacefully?
[them] Settled, at any rate, and everyone's pretending they backed the winner.
[us] What came of the peace talks?
[them,their:peace] Peace with {PEACEWITH}, for now, and everyone's holding their breath.
[them,!their:peace] Nothing yet that anyone at home would call peace.
[us,their:peace] Then I hope it lasts.
[us,!their:peace] Then maybe next time.
[them] The rush is over, and the hills are full of holes and empty pockets.
[us] Did anyone get rich?
[them] Hardly anyone, and the rest are telling everyone how close they came.
[them] The last of the great harvest is in, and the barns are fit to burst.
[us] A good winter ahead, then.
[them] The best in years, if the mice don't get there first.
[them] {ENDED} is over, and the roads are quiet again.
[us] Do you miss the crowds?
[them] I miss the singing, and not one bit of the crowds.
[them] That's the end of {ENDED}, and trade is back to its usual crawl.
[us,role:trader] For you or for us?
[us] Is that good or bad?
[them] Depends whether you were buying or selling.
[them] Is it always this dark at midday out here?
[us] It's an eclipse, it'll pass.
[them,their:tribal] My people would be beating drums to bring the sun back.
[them] I'll hold you to that.
[them] Lightning and not a drop of rain, it's an ugly sky.
[us] Watch for fires, they start fast in this.
[them] I'll keep away from anything dry.
[us] Nothing with a wire in it works today, the sun's seen to that.
[them,their:hightech] My gear's gone dead too, it's just heavy now.
[them] Then it's a good day for doing things by hand.
[them] This haze stings the eyes, how do you stand it?
[us] We don't, much, we stay in when we can.
[them] Then I'll keep a cloth over my face until I'm out of it.
[them] The ground's dry as bone all the way here.
[us] It's hard on everything that grows.
[them,their:tribal] The rain spirits have gone visiting somewhere else.
[them] It'll break, it always does.
[them] There's a weight in the air today, like a headache that isn't mine.
[us] A psychic drone, it's got some of us on edge too.
[them] Then let's be gentle with each other until it passes.
[them] I've walked through a lot of weather, but never rain like this.
[us] Stay out of it, it does things to people's tempers.
[them] I'll keep out of it as best I can.
[them] Everything's gone the color of ash today.
[us] It'll lift, sooner or later.
[them] I hope sooner, it gets into a person's mood.
[them] They say the dead don't rest under a sky like this.
[us] They don't, so stay close to the living tonight.
[them] I'll sleep with one eye open.
[them] I've never seen a dark like this, it swallows the lamplight.
[us] Stay in the light, whatever you do.
[them] You don't need to tell me twice.
[us] Has the fallout reached {TOWN} too?
[them,their:tribal] The sky sickness is everywhere, the elders keep the children inside.
[them] As far as I know, it's over the whole region.
[us] Then we're all waiting it out together.
[them] {PEACEA} and {PEACEB} have made peace, did you hear?
[us] I hadn't, will it hold?
[them,their:tribal] As long as the young ones remember who started it.
[them] It'll hold until it doesn't, like every peace.
[us] Still, it's one war fewer.
[us] Whose side are your people on, {WARA} or {WARB}?
[them,their:empire] The Empire's, which is the only side it ever takes.
[them] Our own, which is the only side that's ever done us any good.
[us] Fair enough.
[us] Do you think the peace with {PEACEWITH} will last?
[them,their:medieval] As long as the lords keep their oaths, which is to say, ask me in a year.
[them] As long as nobody gives anyone a reason, which is asking a lot.
[us] I'll ask again next time, then.
[them] Do, and hope I've good news.
[them] I hear you've taken on {QUESTNOW}.
[us] We have, and we mean to see it through.
[them,their:tribal] Then the elders will be watching how it goes.
[them] People at home will be watching how it goes.
[us] Then we'd better not disappoint them.
[us] Is there anything your people need doing?
[them] There's {QUEST}, if anyone here is willing.
[us] We'll think on it.
[them,role:trader] Think fast, these things don't wait for long.
[them] Don't think too long, it won't wait forever.
[them] Folk at home still talk about how you saw {DEEDNAME} through.
[us] It was worth doing.
[them,their:tribal] It is told at the fire, and the children ask for it again.
[them] It was worth a lot to us.
[them] Some at home still grumble about {WRONGNAME}.
[us] It didn't go the way we hoped.
[them] It didn't go the way anyone hoped, but we're still talking, aren't we?
